doc_mentions.claim: Section "Selecting categories in-process". In-process captures (runtron --trace FILE, --trace-gen FILE, the SIGUSR1 tracer when TRACE_FILE names a path, and rinzler FUSE captures that set no categories) take their category selection from TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES (lines 267-272).

Example: TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES="+memory,-loading,-driver-detail". The value is a comma-separated list of category names, each with a sign. "+" adds to enabled_categories and "-" to disabled_categories. A trailing "*" is a prefix wildcard and an exact name beats a wildcard (lines 279-290). Unset or empty changes nothing. An entry with no sign, a wildcard not at the end, or an unknown name aborts the run at startup. Setting it for a "traced" session is an error that ends rinzler (lines 292-304).
In-process captures enable the memory category with TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES=+memory.

A FUSE capture start that sets no categories uses TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES, as set when rinzler starts. A bad value fails every such capture until rinzler restarts with a good one. Line 68 points to the README.perfetto.md section.
OS events need the SIGUSR1 workflow on a rinzler with TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES unset.
rinzler-capture.sh refuses a rinzler started with TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES.

With TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES unset or empty, the in-process backend keeps the default Perfetto tags, which omit driver-detail and memory. Set it for in-process category selection (line 98). Lines 288 and 388 repeat this.

rederive.audience_reason: It switches a main performance feature of rinzler and runtron on a running system, and the program logs it by name at model load.
rederive.default: Unset: each model uses its compiled default, and the engagement point is token position 127 (MIN_TOK_IDX_FOR_HWATTN, h/libpos.hpp:91). The default is on when the model plugin defines force_hw_attn = true, and off otherwise (h/tron/models/model.hpp:761-767). The ingest code generator writes force_hw_attn = true into every model struct that it generates (ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:258). No other file under h/ or src/ defines force_hw_attn, so hand-written plugins default to off.
rederive.effect: Chooses between hardware attention (on the FPGA cards) and software attention (on the CPU) for each eligible model. With N >= 128 it also raises the engagement point. Software attention serves every token position below the engagement point. Engagement point = 128 * (N div 128 + 1) - 1. That is the smallest number of the form k*128 - 1 that is >= N. N = 1 to 127 gives 127 (same as the default). N = 128 to 255 gives 255. N = 1000 gives 1023. (128 is POS_PER_PAGE, the token positions in one hardware K/V page, h/libpos.hpp:78.)
rederive.empty_value: An empty value is not the same as unset. std::atol reads it as 0. Hardware attention is then off for every model, also for ingested models whose default is on.
rederive.how_to_check: Log lines at level info, printed once for each model state when it is created. ON: "HW attention enabled for model '<id>': max_layers=.. engagement=<point> kv_slot_extent=.. <config> (USE_HW_ATTN)" (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1861-1868). The field engagement= shows the engagement point in effect. The suffix is (USE_HW_ATTN) when the variable is set, and (model default) when it is unset. OFF: "HW attention disabled for model '<id>': <reason>" (model.hpp:1907). The reason USE_HW_ATTN=0 means that the variable is set and parsed to 0 or less. The log prints the fixed text USE_HW_ATTN=0 for every such value, also for true or an empty value. It never prints the real text of the variable. The reason 'default off for this model' means that the variable is unset and the model default is off. Other reasons name EMEM, the activation format, or 'no POS devices available' (model.hpp:1890-1906). When an earlier check fails, one of these lines appears instead and the variable is not consulted: 'HW-attention not available for pipeline stage' (model.hpp:1794), 'HW-attention not available for this model. Will use SW-only path.' (model.hpp:1804), 'HW-attention scale is not representable on device' (model.hpp:1809), 'HW-attention has no eligible operations' (model.hpp:1837). No statistic that shows the value was found.
rederive.interactions: No command-line flag of rinzler or runtron sets or overrides it (no such option name in src/rinzler.cpp or src/runtron.cpp). The variable cannot force hardware attention. Each of these checks keeps a model on software attention, whatever the value. (1) A pipeline stage that does not hold the embedding layer (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1791). (2) A model shape that is not eligible, or an EAGLE model (plugin flag is_eagle) (model.hpp:745-759, 1803). (3) An attention scale that the device cannot represent (model.hpp:1808). (4) EMEM (the FPGA memory for the Q.K dot products) too small for one shard (model.hpp:779). (5) Activations that are not DMA-able BF16 (model.hpp:785, 795-797). (6) No POS device (FPGA card) found (model.hpp:1815-1816). (7) No eligible attention operation (model.hpp:1836). Checks 4 and 5 run before the variable is consulted (model.hpp:769-786). The decision is read once per process, so a change needs a restart. The log text at model.hpp:1794-1800 says that a pipeline matches a single host byte for byte only when both run software attention (USE_HW_ATTN=0 on every stage) under deterministic mode. Other reads in the same code path, each with its own entry: TRON_HWATTN_EARLY_LAUNCH_MIN_B (model.hpp:113) and TRON_HWATTN_COMPOUND_SPLIT (model.hpp:2912). The value of TRON_HWATTN_COMPOUND_SPLIT is read and then ignored (model.hpp:2916-2918). Two setters exist in the checkout. t/CMakeLists.txt:598 sets USE_HW_ATTN=1 for the test t_heterogeneous_scheduler. bin/hugepage_exhaustion_repro.py:217 sets it from its --hw-attn option (default 1) for the rinzler process it starts. The proxy and mock scheduler sources (src/tron/scheduler/proxy.cpp, mock.cpp) contain no call to these helpers.
rederive.invalid_value: The code prints no error and no warning. Text with no leading digit is read as 0, so true, on and yes all turn hardware attention OFF. A negative number also turns it off. Text that starts with digits uses those digits (1x is read as 1). For the engagement point, a value above 1073741824 (2^30) is capped to 2^30 (hw_attn_config.cpp:28). The code does not guard a number outside the range of the C type long.

rederive.values: Decimal integer N, parsed with std::atol (src/tron/models/hw_attn_config.cpp:24). N <= 0: hardware attention (attention computed on the FPGA cards) is off for every model. N >= 1: hardware attention is on for every eligible model, and N also sets the engagement point (the first 0-based token position of a sequence that hardware attention serves). std::atol follows the C library rules: it skips leading white space, accepts one sign, and stops at the first character that is not a digit. So 200k is read as 200 and 1.9 is read as 1. Text with no leading digit is read as 0.

rederive.default: Unset: make_tokenizer chooses (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:2206). When the model directory holds a file tokenizer.json, it returns the Rust Hugging Face tokenizer (lines 1890-1896). When the file is absent, it returns the Python tokenizer (lines 1898-1903). When the file exists but the Rust library cannot load it, the code still returns the Rust tokenizer object: the test at line 1893 checks a pointer from std::make_shared (line 1916), which is never null. The log then shows the error 'Failed to load HuggingFace tokenizer from <path>' (line 991) and after it the info line 'Successfully created HuggingFace Rust tokenizer' (line 1894). That object logs 'HuggingFace tokenizer is null' and returns no tokens on encode (lines 1331-1334). Its decode_stream asserts that the token id is inside the vocabulary cache (lines 1627-1628), and that cache is filled only after a successful load (line 1236 onward). The warning at line 1897 and the Python fallback after it are not reached in that case.
rederive.disagreement: Parsing, accepted values, the empty value and the priority of VALIDATE_TOKENIZERS agree. Three points differ. (1) Default: the inventory says the Python tokenizer is used when tokenizer.json is absent or does not load. The code reaches the Python tokenizer only when the file is absent. When the file exists but does not load, the test at src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:1893 is still true, because std::make_shared (line 1916) never returns null. The code returns a Rust tokenizer object that encodes nothing (lines 989-994, 1331-1334). (2) Effect: the inventory names only the speed cost. It omits that the Python tokenizer has no special-token list, which makes rinzler refuse reasoning_budget_message requests with HTTP 400, disables the ATEM protocol, and drops the arguments token id of named-argument tool calls. It also omits the failure paths (abort at line 462, null handle at lines 1926-1928). (3) Audience: the inventory says developer-debug. This derivation says operator. That point is a judgment, not a code fact.
rederive.effect: Forces the Python tokenizer for every model directory, also when tokenizer.json exists. The Python tokenizer runs a helper program as a child process: once at creation to load the vocabulary (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:469), and once for every encode call (line 568). Decode uses the vocabulary held in memory. This tokenizer reports no special-token list (special_token_ids returns nullopt, lines 279-281). Three results follow in rinzler. (1) A request with reasoning_budget_tokens and a non-empty reasoning_budget_message, on a model with a reasoning close sequence, is refused with HTTP 400 (h/rinzler/reasoning-budget-setup.hpp:83-86, src/rinzler/hf-token-processor.cpp:499-509, src/rinzler.cpp:3630-3636). (2) The ATEM protocol (the channel-marker chat protocol in src/rinzler/atem-protocol.cpp) is disabled for the model (atem-protocol.cpp:43-48). (3) A named-argument tool-call marker gets no arguments token id (src/rinzler/chat-template-tool-call.cpp:79-84).

rederive.interactions: VALIDATE_TOKENIZERS is tested first (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:2193). When VALIDATE_TOKENIZERS is on, USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER is ignored. TRON_TOKENIZE_PY gives the path of the helper program. When TRON_TOKENIZE_PY is unset or empty, the path is bin/tokenize_py relative to the current working directory (lines 448-454). If the helper program does not exist, a TRON_ASSERT stops the process (line 462). If the vocabulary child process fails or prints nothing, the constructor throws (lines 476-480). make_python_tokenizer then logs 'Failed to create fallback python tokenizer' and returns a tokenizer with a null handle (lines 1926-1928). make_cached_tokenizer stores and returns it with no check (lines 2204-2209), and tokenizer::encode calls through the handle with no check (line 310). The choice is cached for each model directory for the life of the process (lines 2180-2185, 2208), so a change needs a restart. In rinzler the tokenizer factory is not called for a model whose id contains gpt-oss. Such a model uses Harmony encoding (src/rinzler.cpp:2020, 2134, 2171). The variable has no effect for those models in rinzler. runtron calls the factory for every model (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:1496). No command-line flag of rinzler or runtron selects the tokenizer type. USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER is the only switch that selects the plain Python tokenizer when tokenizer.json exists.

rederive.disagreement: Parsing, accepted values, the empty value, the default, the priority over USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER and the audience agree. Two points differ. (1) Effect: the inventory says each call 'returns the Python result'. For encode the wrapper returns the Python tokens plus BOS and EOS ids that the wrapper itself picks (config value, else token ids 128000 and 128001), and it does not apply add_bos_token (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:1941-1974, 1982-1998). It can also append its EOS id to the stop-token list (lines 2078-2089). So the mode can change the prompt tokens. (2) Notes: the inventory says 'Both tokenizers must load, or a TRON_ASSERT aborts the process (line 1944)'. The assert tests the handle pointers only. The Rust pointer is never null (std::make_shared, line 1916), so a failed Rust load does not trip this assert. Only a failed Python tokenizer does.
rederive.effect: Creates a validation tokenizer that holds a Rust tokenizer and a Python tokenizer for the model directory (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:1939-1940). Each call runs both and compares the results. A mismatch is logged at level error for encode, decode, decode_stream, vocabulary size and stop tokens, and at level warn for the BOS and EOS text and ids (BOS and EOS are the begin-of-sequence and end-of-sequence tokens). The call returns the Python result. The mode is not neutral for the output. encode asks both tokenizers for tokens without BOS and EOS, and then adds its own BOS id and EOS id when the caller asks for them (lines 1982-1998). These ids come from bos_token_id and eos_token_id in tokenizer_config.json, then from the model config, and otherwise from the fixed default token ids 128000 and 128001 (lines 1941-1974). The add_bos_token setting of tokenizer_config.json is not applied on this path. The Rust and Python tokenizers do apply it (lines 558 and 1356). When the two stop-token lists are equal, the wrapper also appends its own EOS id if the list lacks it (lines 2078-2089). Every encode starts a Python child process (line 568), so the mode is slow.

Mismatch lines start with 'Core tokenization mismatch' (line 1985), 'Validation decode mismatch' (line 2028), 'Validation decode_stream mismatch' (line 2046), 'Vocab size mismatch' (line 2064) or 'Stop tokens mismatch' (line 2075).

It needs the Python helper program: TRON_TOKENIZE_PY, or bin/tokenize_py relative to the current working directory (lines 448-454). A missing helper program stops the process with a TRON_ASSERT (line 462). The TRON_ASSERT at lines 1944-1945 tests the two handle pointers. The Rust pointer comes from std::make_shared (line 1916) and is never null, so this assert stops the process only when the Python tokenizer could not be created (lines 1926-1928). The wrapper returns the Rust special-token list (lines 2153-2157) but builds its lexicon from per-token decode (lines 283-297).
